record.paper_title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows
record.original_question: Given a finite poset P, is the jump number of P at most k, where the jump number is the minimum possible number of consecutive incomparable pairs in a linear extension of P?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P = (X, ≤) be a finite partially ordered set. A linear extension of P is a total order L = x_1 < x_2 < ⋯ < x_n on X such that x_i ≤ x_j in P implies i ≤ j. For a linear extension L, a jump is an index i ∈ {1, …, n−1} such that x_i and x_{i+1} are incomparable in P. The jump number s(P) of P is the minimum, over all linear extensions L of P, of the number of jumps in L.

The Jump Number problem is the following parameterized decision problem:
- Input: a finite poset P and a positive integer k.
- Parameter: k.
- Question: Is s(P) ≤ k?

Determine whether this parameterized problem is fixed-parameter tractable, i.e., decide whether there exists an algorithm solving it in time f(k) · |P|^{O(1)} for some computable function f.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is fixed-parameter tractable. Kratsch and Kratsch (IPEC 2013, "The Jump Number Problem: Exact and Parameterized") gave an O*(2^w) algorithm parameterized by the width w of the poset. Since any poset with jump number at most k has width at most k+1 (a linear extension with k jumps decomposes the ground set into k+1 chains), FPT in the width parameter immediately yields FPT in the jump-number parameter k, with running time O*(2^k). Hence the original question parameterized by k is solved (positively).

status_evidence.title: The Jump Number Problem: Exact and Parameterized
status_evidence.snippet: Fixed-parameter tractability in terms of width w by an O*(2^w) time algorithm and an almost-linear kernel for Jump Number on interval orders parameterized by the number of jumps.
status_evidence.claim: Jump Number is FPT parameterized by poset width; since width ≤ jumpnumber+1, it is also FPT parameterized by k.

status_evidence.title: Exact exponential algorithms for two poset problems (arXiv:1912.13117)
status_evidence.snippet: Jump number can be solved in arbitrary posets in time O(1.824^n), improving previous bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent work confirms classical NP-hardness and provides exact/parameterized algorithms for jump number.
